models.inverse_notes: Inverse f=1/T requires T>0 and has one positive root. T=2.5 s gives f=0.4 Hz; substituting yields 1/0.4=2.5 s. limitations: Zero frequency corresponds to no finite repeating cycle and cannot be assigned an infinite scalar period.

references.method: Published Example 16.1(b) gives 0.50 s, retained as expected. Half its final 0.01 s reporting step gives 0.005 s tolerance; this is an arithmetic example, not measured uncertainty.

models.inverse_notes: Inverse n=299792458/v requires 0<v<=299792458 in this n>=1 profile; one positive root, c remains fixed. v=149896229 m/s yields n=2 and forward substitution returns 149896229. models.inverse_notes: Solve C_1 given finite f,n_l,n_m,C_2: C_1=C_2+1/[f*(n_l/n_m-1)]; require f!=0,n_m>=1,n_l>=1,n_l!=n_m and reconstructed original guards. C_2=C_1-1/[f*(n_l/n_m-1)] under the same exclusions. Solve n_l given f,n_m,C_1,C_2: n_l=n_m*(1+1/[f*(C_1-C_2)]), require f!=0,C_1!=C_2,n_m>=1 and reconstructed n_l>=1. Check f=0.5,n_l=1.5,n_m=1,C_2=0 -> C_1=4; reinsert to obtain f=0.5. C_1=0 is individually admissible when the other curvature and index contrast give nonzero power. If n_l=n_m, no finite f determines either curvature, since zero power holds for all curvatures; C_1=C_2 is the same infinite-focus singularity. These affine/reciprocal inverse directions have one root when admissible; n_m inverse and other directions not separately assessed.
limitations: n_l=n_m or C_1=C_2 makes optical power zero; a finite focal length is unavailable, so the record rejects that finite-output view rather than declaring the transparent system unphysical.
Ignores finite-thickness correction, aberrations and chromatic variation beyond the supplied wavelength-specific indices.
First and second curvatures cannot be swapped without changing the element orientation and sign mapping.

references.method: Published Example 2.3 solves radius=22 cm from f=-20 cm, n_l=1.55,n_m=1.00. Use inverse radii -1/0.22,+1/0.22 as inputs and preserve the given f=-0.20 m as expected. The source is an inverse textbook calculation, not independent experimental evidence. Tolerance 0.005 m is half the 1 cm reporting increment of -20 cm.

Independent synthetic paraxial ray construction: parallel ray at height 0.001 m, first surface radius 0.25 m. Normal slope is -0.004; incident angle relative normal is 0.004, refracted is 0.004/1.5, so internal slope is -0.00133333333333. Plane exit multiplies small ray slope by index ratio 1.5, producing -0.002; height reaches zero after 0.001/0.002=0.5 m. This traces two interfaces, not the serialized focal expression. Exact synthetic inputs, tolerance for binary rounding.

models.inverse_notes: Solve d_o from n_1,n_2,R,d_i: d_o=n_1*R*d_i/[(n_2-n_1)*d_i-n_2*R], require n_1,n_2>=1,R!=0,d_i!=0, nonzero displayed denominator, reconstructed d_o>0 and original guards. Check (1,1.5,0.1,0.6) gives 0.4; source equation then has 1/0.4+1.5/0.6=5=(1.5-1)/0.1. Solve R=numer/denom where numer=(n_2-n_1)*d_o*d_i and denom=n_1*d_i+n_2*d_o, require nonzero denom and resulting R!=0 plus original guards. Same example yields R=0.1. For n_1=n_2 and d_i=-d_o, numerator and denominator both zero: any admissible nonzero R is compatible and cannot be recovered; other conjugates inconsistent. These are unique roots otherwise subject to stated guards; refractive-index inversions not assessed.
limitations: Not a complete thick lens or dielectric sphere model: a later exit interface requires separate modeling.
At the object focus the transmitted rays are parallel, so finite d_i is unavailable.
Paraxial image location ignores aberrations and does not give image intensity, transmission, reflection fraction or diffraction.

references.method: Independent small-angle ray geometry at height h=0.001 m: incoming slope=h/0.4=0.0025; local normal slope=-h/0.1=-0.010. Incident relative-normal angle 0.0125 becomes 0.00833333333333 in index 1.5. Outgoing slope -0.00166666666667 reaches the axis after 0.001/0.00166666666667=0.6 m. Oracle uses refraction and ray intersection, not serialized conjugate equation. Synthetic paraxial values, tolerance covers repeating decimals.

variables.context: Same single spherical interface and optical axis, incident medium 1 and transmitted semi-infinite medium 2, same wavelength and medium states. Real-is-positive convention with a real object d_o>0; d_i>0 real image in outgoing medium and d_i<0 virtual image on incident side. R>0 convex toward real object, R<0 concave toward it.
variables.definition: Phase refractive index in the transmitted semi-infinite medium.
variables.domain: Finite at least one for ordinary transparent-medium profile at the same wavelength.

variables.context: Same single spherical interface and optical axis, incident medium 1 and transmitted semi-infinite medium 2, same wavelength and medium states. variables.definition: Signed spherical-interface radius, positive with center in outgoing medium for the real-object incidence convention.
variables.domain: Finite nonzero signed radius; plane boundary requires a curvature parameterization or limiting treatment.
